messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] region=euw2 severity=page type=egress-errors spike detected: 4xx/5xx ratio > 30% and routefailures observed in route53 healthchecks, paging oncall (policy: immediate)

carmen: on it. seeing the same in console, spikes started ~10:34UTC. Is this customer impacting?

miguel: i'm seeing ~20% of outgoing connections to external partner endpoints failing with TCP RSTs. NAT gw metrics look noisy.

carmen: confirming customer impact: embeddings calls to model-redwood-embed-1 in euw2 are timing out for ~25% of requests, some fall through to retry and increase latency.

sre_jay: @carmen good find. can you post the command output for the route53 healthchecks? wondering if healthchecks are flapping or probes are missing telemetry.

carmen: paste:
```
aws route53 get-health-check-status --health-check-id hc-0a1b2c3d
Status: FAILING
LastChecked: 2026-03-15T10:34:45Z
ConsecutiveFailures: 7
```

ops_anya: CloudWatch egress network metrics from NATs show a sharp drop in packets forwarded around the same time. Could be an AZ-level network fabric issue.

samir: overlay logs from the serving nodes show a bunch of `connect: network unreachable` errors, and KV cache RPCs failing with timeout. excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:35:12Z] serve-023 egress: dial tcp 52.35.12.66:443: connect: network is unreachable
[2026-03-15T10:35:13Z] cache: write timeout to meta-store (rpc timeout)
```

elaine-cs: flagged a handful of customers asking about request failures. CS is triaging escalations, several paying customers hit retries. pls keep me updated on ETA for mitigation.

sre_jay: quick mitigation idea: failover egress for critical routes to euw1 via cross-region NAT while we investigate. That will route traffic differently but reduce domain-specific fallout. Running impact analysis now.

miguel: agree, but need to be careful about rate limits and latency bump. we should only re-route model hosting endpoints and not internal infra traffic.

carmen: i'm going to flip traffic for `/models/*/infer` on the api-router for customer-tier=paid to fallback region. patching route policy now. command: 
```
# update traffic policy
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/route-policies -d '{"match":"/models/.*/infer","selector":"tier=paid","fallback":"euw1"}'
```

infra-bot: deploy started: route-policy patch by carmen (id rp-7623) — rolling update to 12 routers.

sre_jay: while that rolls, please disable probe-suppression that may be hiding telemetry — I want raw healthchecks. runbook step: `scripts/probes/disable_suppression.sh --region euw2`

ops_anya: suppression disabled. verifying CloudWatch synthetic checks now. we got a bunch of synthetic-heartbeat misses earlier; those are counting now.

miguel: after policy change: initial metrics show 70% of paid model traffic now hitting euw1 successfully. error rate for paid customers dropped to ~3% in the last 2m. good.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] Paging status: mitigated for paid-model-traffic via fallback routing. investigation ongoing for root cause (euw2 egress fabric).

elaine-cs: passing to CS: notifying impacted customers of failover and that we have partial mitigation. asking for any contracts that require full euw2 routing — will coordinate.

sre_jay: next steps: 1) collect BGP/NIC counters from euw2 border routers 2) check provider peering events 3) confirm NAT gateway resource limits not exhausted 4) ensure probe coverage isn't suppressed in future incidents. I've created an incident checklist ticket: INC-6621.

carmen: collecting dumps now: `tcpdump -i eth0 host 52.35.12.66 and port 443 -c 10000 -w /tmp/egress-dump.pcap` and `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=euw2*`

miguel: found a suspicious NAT gateway metric: high `ActiveConnections` followed by abrupt `NetworkOut` drop. can someone confirm whether autoscaling for NATs failed?

ops_anya: checking autoscaling groups for nat-eni workers — ASG show scale-in events at 10:33UTC due to a faulty scale policy. opening an ops PR to change scale policy to conservative thresholds.

samir: adding note: we also saw Route53 healthcheck timeouts at the same time which may have triggered DNS-based failovers in some customers — that could amplify traffic patterns.

incident-bot: [ACTION] handoff scheduled in 25m to night-shift oncall (sre_nina). please document state in the incident ticket before handoff.

sre_jay: documenting: mitigation applied (partial), fallback routing active for paid model endpoints, customer impact reduced. root cause suspected: combination of NAT autoscaling misfire + provider-level peering perturbation causing egress path loss. telemetry gap caused by probe suppression made diagnosis slower. next: provider support ticket, NAT autoscaling policy fix, expand synthetic probe coverage, add alert on `ActiveConnections` spike followed by `NetworkOut` drop.

carmen: uploading PSR (packet captures + logs) to the incident ticket.

elaine-cs: CS will follow up with impacted customers and offer credits where appropriate. keep me looped for final RCA wording.

miguel: provider replied to initial support case: "We're investigating an internal fabric flap in euw2 affecting a subset of NAT IPs. Recommend routing failover while we remediate."

ops_anya: put a temporary guardrail to prevent ASG scale-in actions during active network alerts. adding automated tag `incident_in_progress=true` to suppress scale-in. will revert after postmortem.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE?] mitigation stable for 15m, no new pages. if no regressions, will move to monitoring state.

sre_jay: proceeding to handoff. handoff notes: timeline, mitigations, commands executed, artifacts uploaded. @sre_nina you'll find the incident ticket INC-6621 with next steps.

elaine-cs: thanks all, CS is drafting customer comms now. ETA for RCA will be after provider confirms fix and we complete postmortem. :thumbsup:

carmen: signing off for now, leaving lead to @sre_jay for handoff. ping me if anything escalates.
